With allegiances on the line, will you rise as one worthy to be followed? Forge great armies in your camps, construct wonders, and keep a watchful eye on the road ahead. Will you reign as the most spirited champion of the ancient world? The aim of Spirited is to be the player with the most Spirit after the Final Battle. Players gain Spirit through Marching with Clans to forge Allegiances, fighting in Battles, and by Building Wonders. The Clan Draw Pile contains 3 Passing of Time Cards, which when Revealed, advance the game 1 step closer towards the Final Battle. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary ======================================== WHAT IS THE GAME? Spirited is a competitive card game for 2-6 players. You play as ancient civilizations competing for Spirit (victory points). Whoever has the most Spirit when the game ends wins. You earn Spirit three ways: - Marching — collecting sets of clan cards to claim Allegiances (loyalty badges with medals) - Battles — scoring your medals during periodic battle events - Building Wonders — spending one card of every clan to grab a wonder card ======================================== YOUR PLAY AREA Every player has a City Board with cards around it in four zones: ROAD (above your board) Faceup cards arrive here from the draw pile. This is your "public" zone — other players can mess with it. Cards of the same clan get stacked together. CAMPS (below your board) Up to 2 piles of cards you've collected from your Road. Each camp holds only one clan type. You cannot freely move cards between camps or combine them. Camps are safe from opponents. You use camps to March. HAND Cards you've picked up privately. Safe from opponents — nobody can look at them. No hand limit normally, but you discard down to 5 during Battles. SPIRIT TOKENS Your score. Kept visible to everyone. You can freely exchange tokens of equal value with the supply. ======================================== RALLY vs RECRUIT Almost everything in the game revolves around these two actions: RALLY = Move a faceup card from your Road into your Hand. Keeps it private and flexible, but doesn't help you March. RECRUIT = Move a faceup card from your Road into one of your Camps. The camp must be empty, contain only facedown cards, or already have at least one card of the same clan. Builds toward Marching but commits the card to a specific camp. ======================================== TURN STRUCTURE Every turn follows the same structure: STEP 1 — ROAD CHECK (mandatory, every turn) a) If you have fewer than 2 faceup cards on your Road, draw from the deck onto your Road until you have exactly 2. b) If any clan has 3 or more faceup cards on your Road, that clan has hit its Overrun Limit. You must Rally cards from that clan until they drop below the limit. STEP 2 — CHOOSE ONE ACTION Option A: SCOUT 1. You may Play 1 card from your Hand (resolve its effect, then discard it). 2. Rally or Recruit 1 faceup card from your Road. 3. Summon — draw 2 cards onto your Road, then check for Overrun. Option B: BUILD A WONDER 1. Spend 1 card of each of the 7 clans in the game. Cards can come from your Road (faceup only), Camps (faceup only), or Hand. 2. Discard the 7 cards used. 3. Take 1 of the 3 Wonder cards from the Main Board. Gain the Spirit shown on it and resolve its effect. A new Wonder is drawn to replace it. 4. Summon — draw 2 cards onto your Road, then check for Overrun. Option C: MARCH 1. Use cards in your Camps to forge Allegiances (see Marching section below). 2. Gain Spirit equal to the medal values you just collected. 3. Regroup — discard ALL cards from your Road and Camps, then draw 2 cards onto your Road. community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] the game got repetitive fast. there didn't seem to be any interesting build up and you were just gaining 1 card a turn (sometimes not even) toward a build or allegiance until you had enough to score it. then you had to start over  There was no build up of any sort of engine or combo. Buildings were just ability ways to score points or very minor one time effect  left a lot to be desired

[Rating: 3/10] This didn't do much for me...decisions seemed to be largely obvious and at least the cards we were playing with didn't offer much to play at the start of one's turn.  It was just an endless cycle of build up, "buy" something for a few points, reset everything and start over again...not my type of game.

[Rating: 3/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  I didn't much care for this game - felt like build up, trade in and cycle over again and again. There was also some treading water in there and dead turns. Meh.

[Rating: 3/10] Played at 2p, which seems to be the worst player count. But boy did this make you feel rather innefective and susceptible to luck of the draw. Touts a lot of interaction but limited avenues to really do anything to/with others. May be that other factions help with this but pff. Not interested in spending more time on this.

[Rating: 3/10] Kind of a mess. Lot of weird rules that are just there to make game unique or maybe unnecessary complicated. General play is pretty boring, nothing exciting happens.

[Rating: 3/10] - Fairly dull set collection and scoring based on quantity or getting a whole set to buy a building. - Uninteractive feel - yes there is SOME interaction, but it's quite light and inconsequential, especially as it's mostly driven by: - HEAVY luck factor: you can have just one card in your row and bust to two or more cards of that same type coming out (yes, this happened to me on my first playthrough). - Game is boring - no tension, your decisions feel mostly decided/forced by your card flips. - Feels too long for a game with low interaction, low agency and high RNG. If this played in 15 minute

[Rating: 3/10] Turns feel fairly repetitive after the initial 20 minutes of game, and as the card/allegiances powers are a bit bland, the flow of the game feels monotone. Even getting the wonders does not feel "triumphant", it feels procedural.

[Rating: 4/10] Seems painfully slow and repetitive. Too long for such uninteresting mechanics.  May be amusing to see how the Shem and Gaphil fanboys try to excite themselves over this one.

[Rating: 4/10] very simple set collection game pretty boring barely a game (!), limited agency lots of rules headache for as simple as it is not much player interaction  artworks are ok, although it's very weird to pair up anthropomorphic animals with nationalities, even historic ones, they should have gone with fantasy race names for all graphic design could be better, especially the card backs

[Rating: 4/10] first Garphill game that nothing feels right. I am not interested in anthropomorphic animal civilizations, alright, but is the gameplay good? Sadly there is nothing here remotely interesting in the mechanisms. Too bad...

[Rating: 4/10] I am reminding myself that 4-star ratings are described - by BGG itself - as "not so good but could play again." Which for me is perfect: "the BGA digital implementation is not so good but I could play this again... if someone else down the road acquires a physical copy and brought it to a game night (and there weren't any other game alternatives.)"  So take the above context into consideration if you read this "not for me" review of SPIRITED.   That said, I think the digital implementation does not help to convince one who might be on the fence to dig deeper or pursue this game in crowdfundin

[Rating: 4/10] Initial BGA impressions are not good.  Could play better in person, but so far my least favorite game from Garphill.
